content:
DART changed Dimorphos’s orbit over time—not all at once.

Before the impact, Dimorphos took 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit the larger asteroid Didymos. Immediately afterward, its orbital period was 11 hours, 22 minutes and 37 seconds: 32 minutes and 42 seconds shorter.

Over the following weeks, the period continued to shorten. During that same period, Dimorphos also lost more rocky material to space. Its orbit was no longer circular after the impact.

The period eventually settled at 11 hours, 22 minutes and 3 seconds—33 minutes and 15 seconds shorter than before DART struck.
